newsitem.title: USA: Lower bids likely in Plains cattle market - trade.
newsitem.headline: Lower bids likely in Plains cattle market - trade.

text.p: Bids for cattle in U.S. Plains feedlot markets may be lower Monday, possibly at $67.00 to $68.00 per cwt, in the aftermath of Friday's bearishly-construed USDA Cattle-On-Feed report, feedlot sources said.
One Texas feedlot manager said he expects meat packers to bid $67.00 to $68.00 next week, but feedlots will initially hold out for $70.00. Sales late this week were at $69.00.
USDA estimated November 1 feedlot supplies in the seven leading cattle feeding states at 101 percent of a year ago, which exceeded analysts' estimates.

Also, October placements were estimated by USDA at 111 percent of a year ago, which also exceeded analysts' estimates. October marketings at 93 percent of a year ago, came in under analysts' projections, which averaged 97.3 percent in a range of 95.5 to 100 percent.
Several cattle feeders said the weekend weather could be supportive to cash prices. Forecasts called for rain and freezing rain in the Texas Panhandle.
If severe, sources said such weather could stress the cattle and discourage feedlots from selling them until they recover.
Such a scenario could further tighten already-tight numbers of market-ready choice cattle in feedlots, sources said.
